Consider the graph of the function $y=f(x),$ shown above. It consists of a line segment and an arc of a quarter-circle centered at $(0,0)$ with radius $2.$ Find the value of ${\int }_{-3}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-3,0]$ and the arc of a quarter-circle for $x\in [0,2].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =lw \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =6+\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
